newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast spot power weak amid cool weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast spot power weak amid cool weather.

text.p: Spot prices for power in the western U.S. fell slightly today as cooler temperatures reduced demand and utilities moved to shed excess generation.
Daily prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) dipped to $15.00-15.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $15.50-16.00 on Tuesday.
Traders said continued sales during heavy-load hours by the Bonneville Power Administration of excess hydroelectric generation from the Northwest were keeping prices weak.
In addition, BPA offered buyers in both the Northwest and Southwest the option to displace thermal generation with hydro supplies at $9.00 per MWh for Thursday pre-schedulings.
BPA also continued to offer daily surplus firm and non-firm power at $17.00 for peak-demand hours.
"Our loads are way down, so we are starting to shed some generation anyway," noted one California utility trader.
In the Southwest, spot prices eased slightly from earlier this week when a short-term outage of a Wyoming coal-fired power plant created a bout of short covering.
Palo Verde traded around $22.00, down from $24.75-25.00 on Tuesday.
October cash prices also retreated today with COB at $15.90-16.35, down from $16.00-16.50 on Tuesday. October PV was quoted $16.25-17.00, compared with $16.30-16.60 on Tuesday.
